newsitem.title: SPAIN: Madrid stocks close up amid some rate cut hopes.
newsitem.headline: Madrid stocks close up amid some rate cut hopes.

text.p: Madrid stocks closed up on Thursday, underpinned by lower-than-consensus January inflation data and amid some hopes of fresh rate cut tomorrow.
But dealers said the bourse is still wary amid volatility.
The general index rose 2.54 points, 0.53 percent to 477.55 and the Ibex added 22.83 points, 0.42 percent, to 5,458.20.
Santander gained strongly, up 170 pesetas to 9,230 buoyed by an outperform recommendation by Salomon Bros, dealers said.
BBV bank also outstripped indices, up 130 pesetas to 8,750.
Spain's January CPI rose 2.9 percent year on year, versus 3.2 percent in December. Analysts forecast a 3.0 percent rise.
But dealers said short-term the outlook was still uncertain, with price fluctuations scaring investors off.
"Despite excellent inflation data and positive references from other markets, some doubts over the short term have appeared" said one fund manager.

The Bank of Spain's repo auction may produce a rate cut tomorrow, but a narrow consensus expects no change from the present 6.0 percent. On balance, economists think the central bank will opt for caution in an uncertain outlook.
